issues.legal_issue: A corporate successor may claim statutory tenant protection when its predecessor occupied premises under a subsisting licence at the statutory cutoff and the resulting tenancy rights passed to the successor through a statutory transfer of the predecessor’s undertaking.
material_facts: The predecessor occupied the premises under a subsisting leave-and-licence arrangement on the statutory cutoff date.
The statutory amendment deemed a qualifying licensee in occupation on that date to be a tenant.
The predecessor’s undertaking was acquired by the Central Government, and the applicable acquisition provisions treated the Government as tenant in respect of property held by the predecessor.
The tenancy rights were subsequently transferred to a government company, which became the petitioner corporation’s predecessor through amalgamation and a change of name.
The licensor acknowledged that the corporation occupied the premises as successor to the original licensee, and the society sought the corporation’s eviction.
issues.conclusion: The petitioner corporation was entitled to statutory tenant protection. The appellate eviction order and the related proceedings were quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 15A of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, as introduced by Maharashtra Act 17 of 1973, a person occupying premises as a licensee on the statutory cutoff date is deemed to be a tenant. Sections 3 and 5(1) of the Esso (Acquisition of Undertakings in India) Act, 1974 transferred the predecessor’s undertaking rights to the Central Government and deemed the Government to be tenant in respect of property held by the predecessor. Section 7(1) permitted those rights to vest in a government company. The personal character of the original licence did not extinguish the statutory tenancy status already acquired or prevent its transfer through that statutory chain.

rule.if: eviction_claim_against_occupant and predecessor_occupied_under_subsisting_license_at_cutoff and predecessor_undertaking_acquired_by_state and tenancy_rights_transferred_to_government_company and occupant_is_successor_to_rights_holder

predicates.eviction_claim_against_occupant: The proceeding sought to evict an occupant from premises held under a licence.
predicates.predecessor_occupied_under_subsisting_li: The predecessor occupied the premises under a subsisting licence on the legally relevant cutoff date.
predicates.predecessor_undertaking_acquired_by_stat: The state acquired the predecessor’s undertaking, including its relevant rights in the premises.
predicates.tenancy_rights_transferred_to_government: The rights arising from the predecessor’s occupation passed to a government company under the statutory transfer arrangements.
predicates.occupant_is_successor_to_rights_holder: The occupant became the corporate successor to the entity in which those rights had vested.

issues.definition: When an eviction claim concerns an occupant whose predecessor held a subsisting licence at the cutoff, and the resulting rights passed through the state to a government company and then to the occupant as successor, the occupant is entitled to statutory tenant protection.
